newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Jan CPI rises 1.1 pct mo/mo, +5.8 yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Jan CPI rises 1.1 pct mo/mo, +5.8 yr/yr.

text.p: Consumer prices in Slovakia rose 1.1 percent, month-on-month, in January, putting prices 5.8 percent higher over the same period in 1996, the Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) said on Tuesday.
SLOVAK CONSUMER INFLATION Jan 97 Dec 96 Jan 96
Note. SUSR said in a note that due to the changes in the population's expenditure structure, it had revised the formulas for calcuating CPI, using 1995 data as a base.
"In accordance with Eurostat recommendations, the COICOP classification, meaning classification of final household consumption had been worked into the new formula," SUSR said.
Between 1991 and 1996, the index was calculated using January 1989 as a base.

It said that SUSR has added some new items to the basket, and modified others, and that weights calculated had been chosen for the universal consumption basket. The number of basket items has been cut to 708 from previous 836. The new basket will have 11 main divisions and 38 groups.

The new basket divisions are: the foodstuffs and soft drinks (140 items); alcohol, tobacco and pharmaceuticals (12 items), clothes and shoes (125 items); household energy, utilities and fuels (46 items); furniture, household appliances and maintenance (92 items); healthcare (21 items); transportation (54 items); recreation and culture (77 items); education (6 items); hotels, cafes and restaurants (49 items); various goods and services (86 items).
CPI indexes were previously published in four main groups of items -- foodstuffs, non-food items, public catering, services-- and 34 sub-groups.
The weights of the new items will be calculated based on the data monitored from the statistics of household accounts for 1995, SUSR said.
